tier_rationale: Dominion is turn based, and the chosen offline simulator should block at every agent decision, including reactions and discards during the opponent's turn. No game state changes while the model thinks, so Astra may take seconds to a minute or longer without in-game penalty. The rules impose no decision timeout; decision_latency_s is a conservative one-day lower bound used because strict JSON cannot represent infinity, not a game-enforced deadline. Evaluator watchdogs are separate infrastructure policy.

interface.chosen: bot library: local pyminion Python simulator with a blocking JSON decision adaptor (provisional pending source and Python 3.12 validation)
interface.why: A local source-level simulator provides structured state, exact card resolution and programmable opponents without a GUI, service account, runtime network or subscription. Python integrates directly with the evaluator and avoids screen recognition. The recommendation is provisional: outbound research was blocked, no simulator source is cached, and neither its exact API nor Python 3.12 compatibility has been verified. DominionSim through a local Java bridge is the fallback if pyminion cannot pass the documented acceptance checks.
software: A pinned, license-reviewed pyminion wheel or source revision from https://github.com/evanofslack/pyminion or https://pypi.org/project/pyminion/; no release was verified or installed during this study
Complete hashed offline wheelhouse of the chosen pyminion revision's runtime dependencies compatible with CPython 3.12 on Linux x86_64; exact dependencies require inspecting distribution metadata
Optional upstream test dependencies and pytest for adaptor verification; standard-library queues, threading or subprocess and JSON for the bridge
setup_steps: Obtain upstream source, license, metadata and dependency artifacts on a network-enabled provisioning machine, then stage them under the study directory. This session cannot fetch them and found no local copy.

Inspect real game/player/card APIs and tests before implementation: identify all agent decisions, nested attack/reaction prompts, legal-choice helpers, scoring, end conditions, card coverage and every RNG site. Do not assume a ready-made step API or a particular constructor/import path.

Pin a source commit or release and dependencies, save SHA-256 hashes, and build a CPython 3.12/Linux x86_64 wheelhouse. Resolve actual 3.12 incompatibilities with documented patches or use the Java fallback.

In a phase permitted to write the evaluator venv, run its python -m pip install --no-index --find-links ./vendor/wheels --require-hashes -r ./vendor/requirements.lock, then pip check. The study sandbox cannot write this venv and did not install packages.
Run relevant upstream tests with the exact evaluator interpreter. Verify two-player Base setup, source license, cards, shuffles, scoring and termination before selecting the initial whitelist.

Implement a player decision bridge that blocks on a queue or pipe and emits legal JSON prompts. Keep the live game suspended between choices, including choices during the opponent's turn. Map validated option IDs back to engine objects.

Filter observations to the acting player's legal knowledge; hide opponent hand, unrevealed deck order, RNG state and reset seed. Maintain public-event bookkeeping and exact visible-state arithmetic in code.

Implement reproducible reset configuration with explicit kingdom, seat, seed and versioned scripted opponent; isolate global RNG state if necessary. Begin with the base_intro fixture and BM-1 baseline from strategies.md.

Validate nested choice handling, invalid-action nonmutation, privacy, pause behavior, deterministic replay, Province and three-pile endings, Gardens/Curse scoring and turn-count tiebreaks. Run offline baseline matches before expanding the supported card pool. No gameplay code is included in this study.
interface.observation: Proposed adaptor JSON, not an asserted upstream API: episode and decision IDs; viewer/turn owner/decision player; phase and resolving effect; Actions, Buys and money; exact kingdom and remaining Supply; own hand, discard and played cards; deck counts and publicly inferable ownership; opponent counts and public events only; legally known reveals/top cards; a typed pending prompt with legal option IDs and selection constraints; code-computed visible VP and pile pressure. At genuine termination expose full final scores, turns and result. Do not reveal hidden orders, opponent hand or seed.
interface.actions: Answer one pending prompt using its decision ID and legal option IDs, with ordered selections where required. Cover Action play/pass, Treasure play or validated Base-only play-all, buy/stop, constrained gain, trash, discard, topdeck/order, optional reaction and effect-specific mode/target choices. Validate before mutation, return the same prompt on invalid input, then advance forced effects and scripted opponents until the next agent decision or terminal state. Game rules remain owned by the simulator.

scoring: Report agent_vp, opponent_vp, integer vp_margin, outcome and win_score (1 win, 0.5 draw, 0 loss). Final VP includes Curses and variable scoring such as Gardens across all owned zones. Resolve equal VP by fewer turns taken, then shared draw if turns are equal; zero margin can therefore be a win. Track end reason, turns, illegal/fallback counts and truncations separately. Aggregate win rate and mean VP margin across paired seats, kingdoms and opponents; do not replace the requested objectives with money, deck size or a fabricated weighted scalar.
scenarios: Standard two-player 7-Copper/3-Estate starts, ten tested Kingdom piles and normal Supply counts. reset(seed) deterministically varies legal initial shuffles, subsequent shuffle randomness, seat and optionally kingdom/opponent selection from a fixed declared manifest. Include base_intro, chapel_engine, curse_race and gardens_rush fixtures from strategies.md, only after their cards pass conformance checks. Evaluate BM-1, one-Smithy SM-1 and one-Witch WM-1 where applicable, plus a separately validated stronger policy if available. Pair both seats, separate training/held-out seeds, and hold out kingdom combinations as well as shuffle sequences. Never expose seeds to the policy or silently substitute unsupported cards. Record version and scenario configuration for replay.
strategy_summary: Analyze each kingdom for thinning, draw, action capacity, payload, extra buys or gains, attacks and scoring routes before selecting an opening. Efficient money decks with a little terminal draw are a useful baseline, while strong engines require balanced components and a fast enough payoff. Trash early junk while preserving functional economy, and adapt to Witch or Militia pressure rather than treating defense as permanent immunity. Sequence actions to preserve action capacity and improve draws, and monitor shuffle timing without inspecting hidden deck order. Switch from building to scoring according to remaining Provinces, three-pile threats and opponent capability, with exact ending and tiebreak calculations in code. Astra owns strategic planning and adaptation; code owns rules, arithmetic and bookkeeping; optional Jev questions only recognize patterns or rank already legal choices under the plan.
risks: Live web research was blocked: requests to PyPI, GitHub and Dominion Strategy Wiki failed DNS resolution. Citations are concrete reference targets, not successfully accessed evidence; current package/service claims remain unverified.

No pyminion installation or source cache exists in the inspected locations. The target venv has only pip, and the current study sandbox cannot write it. External provisioning with an offline wheelhouse and venv write permission is required.

Pyminion API signatures, release/commit, exact dependency set, license, supported cards and Python 3.12.3 compatibility could not be validated. The recommendation must pass a source and execution gate before implementation readiness is claimed.
A synchronous game loop may have no native step interface. Missing even one nested decision hook can deadlock, auto-play an agent choice or skip a mandatory effect.
An engine may expose hidden hands/deck orders or use global randomness/mutable card objects; observations must filter private information and concurrent/reset games must isolate state.
Unsupported cards, mixed Base editions, wrong gain destinations, three-pile ending timing, Gardens arithmetic or turn-count tiebreak bugs can invalidate results. Restrict scenarios to tested cards.
Offline engine pause time is unlimited; evaluator watchdogs or inference failures must be reported separately. Artificial turn limits are truncations, not legitimate Dominion endings.
Official online clients require connectivity and may restrict automation; proprietary digital clients do not meet the free-software requirement. Neither is the selected interface.
A simple Big Money opponent is exploitable and does not demonstrate general skill. Report results by opponent and use held-out kingdom combinations plus both seats.
